name: NY-11
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent with $2.8M cash vs. $35K for DeCillis
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: Malliotakis combines a Republican-leaning Staten Island district, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge, while prediction markets give her roughly a 96% chance. DeCillis's minimal fundraising gives no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A late Democratic outside-spending surge or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would warrant moving toward a Lean R outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nicole Malliotakis seeks a third term in a Staten Island–based district that leans Republican by about ten points. She has raised $2.75 million and holds $2.77 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Michael DeCillis has raised only about $68,000. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side, and no public general-election polling exists for the race.

Prediction markets price Malliotakis at roughly 96%, and no expert raters list the contest as competitive. The district's partisan lean, incumbency advantage, and lopsided money gap all point the same direction. The forecast expects Malliotakis to win by a comfortable double-digit margin, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
